@note{= Alster 1997 27.1} The rich man's heart is sick, it is very sick indeed -- the man with a troubled heart is sick, he is very sick indeed.
@note{= Alster 1997 27.2} @q{“Why are the interest payments so small?”}
@note{= Alster 1997 27.3} He who carries a light burden can dance.
@note{= Alster 1997 27.4} The conmen are having their say.
@note{= Alster 1997 27.5} People whose houses have been lost turn to their storehouses.
@note{= Alster 1997 27.6} To eat is good. When it comes up again, it is bad.
@note{= Alster 1997 27.7} A troubled mind makes you sick.
@note{= Alster 1997 27.8} On the battlefield plants are torn out.

@note{= Alster 1997 27.9; cf. @xref[t.6.2.3,t623.h75]{6.2.3: UET 6/2 250}} @varh[t6127.v1]{One city does not greet another, but one man greets another. } @vart[t6127.v2,]{@note{1 ms. has instead:} One city does not salute another, but one person salutes another. }

@note{= Alster 1997 27.11} He who found …… was the one who revealed it.
